clue.text: Brooding giant oddly destroyed island into bananas

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the word giant are wiped out, leaving only its even ones

parts.note: Cuba is the Caribbean island

indicators.note: going bananas is going crazy, so the letters of into are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sinister tale of a giant who smashed an island while brooding, the island ending up inside some bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly destroyed' strikes out G, A and T from GIANT, leaving IN; 'bananas' shuffles INTO into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubation is the sitting on eggs to hatch them, which is what a brooding bird does.

clue.text: Useless section of welding is rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards
a section is a piece cut from within, so the letters lie inside the word

explanation.surface: A useless bit of welding is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'section of' takes ELDI from inside WELDING; 'is rejected' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or pointless, as in idle threats, which are of no use.

clue.text: Fine linen in two-thirds of university clubs

indicators.note: only the first six of nine letters are kept, so the final third is lost

parts.note: Cambridge is the English university
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Students at a university's societies wearing fine linen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds of' keeps CAMBRI from CAMBRIDGE, losing its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, dense white cloth, originally made of flax, used for handkerchiefs.

clue.text: British space vessel with provisions for storage

parts.note: room means space
a cup is a drinking vessel
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A British spaceship loaded with supplies for stowing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom cupboard is a small closet used for keeping cleaning equipment stowed.

clue.text: Squeezes cycling crew between leaders in team's new set-up

indicators.note: between says the cycled crew sits inside the leading letters, splitting them
leaders are the front letters of the three words that follow
cycling moves a letter from the front of crew to its back

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: A team reshuffle tightening the squeeze, with a cycling squad among its stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' sends the first letter of the crew to its end; 'between' sets the result after the first leader, before the other two. A rowing eight is a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten something is to squeeze it, drawing it closer and more firmly.

clue.text: Subject's temperature dropped about eye

indicators.note: the abbreviation for temperature is moved lower down and placed about the word's middle

parts.note: a topic is a subject for discussion

explanation.surface: A patient's fever has fallen, according to the eye doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped about' moves the T of TOPIC further down, to between the P and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an old, now humorous, word for the eye itself, the organ of sight.

clue.text: Start prison disturbance

definitions.meaning: to begin to move, to start into action after rest

explanation.surface: A news line about a riot breaking out in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions of one word, read separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir covers all three senses: beginning to move, slang for a jail, and a commotion.

clue.text: Brown meets President, almost showing rage

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: Donald Trump, US President

explanation.surface: A former UK Prime Minister meets the US President, who is almost raging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' suggests Gordon Brown but is just the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a sudden childish fit of temper or bad-tempered outburst.

clue.text: You might get this straight from throne in Buckingham Palace?

definitions.text: You might get this straight from throne in Buckingham Palace?

parts.words: You might get this straight from throne in Buckingham Palace
parts.note: a poker hand of ace-high straight in one suit, read as the royal toilet being flushed

explanation.surface: What happens after the monarch's loo is used, or a top poker hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'throne' is slang for a lavatory, and a poker 'straight' of ten to ace in one suit is the top hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the best possible hand is ace, king, queen, jack and ten of one suit.

clue.text: Member gets over state of uncertainty

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A club member gets past a period of doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is only a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo means being stuck in an unresolved, undecided condition.

clue.text: Receipts over year involving new team

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the reworked team goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: something that is over is gone

indicators.note: new suggests the word team is made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A club's takings across the year, with a new side involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' means finished here, not a cricket over; 'new' scrambles the team, and 'involving' wraps the other pieces round it just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gate money is the total takings from spectators paying at the turnstiles of a sports ground.

clue.text: Making small cocktail of martini, using bottled Asti at the end

indicators.note: bottled means held inside, so the last letter of Asti goes within the mix
a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of martini and using are shaken up
at the end picks out the final letter of the wine's name

explanation.surface: A recipe for a cocktail of martini using some sparkling Italian wine poured in at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail of' mixes the two words; 'bottled' holds the wine's final letter inside the mix. Asti is a sparkling Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Miniaturising is reducing something to a tiny scale, so making it little.

clue.text: Out-of-the-way direction taken by channel-hopper

parts.note: an out-of-the-way place is remote
direction in the sense of management or command is control

explanation.surface: Taking a detour off the beaten track, as advised by someone who keeps switching routes.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV zapper lets a viewer flick between stations, which is what a channel-hopper does.

clue.text: At home, sat mock, previously unwilling

indicators.note: previously says the word for mock comes before the word for sat

parts.note: in means at home
to dis is to disrespect or mock someone
posed, as a model sits for a portrait

explanation.surface: A student at home, having sat a mock exam, was reluctant beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Indisposed can mean disinclined or reluctant, as well as slightly ill.

clue.text: Performance in once jazzy musical composition

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
jazzy suggests a lively reworking, so the letters of once are mixed up

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act or routine on stage

explanation.surface: A show staged in a once-jazzy musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazzy' scrambles the word once as NOCE, and 'in' sets the performance inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a short dreamy piano piece evoking night, as written by Chopin.

clue.text: Mother left animal

parts.note: mamma is a childish word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum walked out, leaving behind a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A mammal is a warm-blooded creature that suckles its young, a kind of beast.

clue.text: Buck maybe takes two seconds when rising on holiday

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top, so backwards
takes means holds within, so the seconds go inside

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, so deer by example
two words for second: S and SEC

explanation.surface: A deer takes a couple of seconds to get up while on vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' puts S and SEC inside DEER for DESSECER, then 'rising' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A body that has recessed has adjourned for a break, as Parliament goes into recess.

clue.text: The setter's stomach rejects large drink

parts.note: the bible is one of the four stomachs of a ruminant, also called the omasum or psalterium

explanation.surface: The setter complains that their stomach will not accept a large drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The bible is the third stomach of a cow, named for its leaf-like folds; 'rejects' removes its L.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to consume liquid, especially alcohol, so it means to drink.

clue.text: Lout turning up in audition put a stop to One Direction, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a yob is a lout or hooligan

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so what follows is judged by its sound

parts.note: banned means put a stop to

explanation.surface: A thug turns up at an audition and halts a famous group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audition' fits the talent-show surface but means the spoken form of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: One Direction was a famous British-Irish pop group of young male singers, an example.

clue.text: Soldiers pull round to enter towers

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: rears in the sense of rises high, towers up

indicators.note: turned round means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to lug is to pull or haul something heavy

explanation.surface: Troops drag something around to get into some fortified towers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towers' is a verb here, rises up, not buildings; 'round' turns the pull backwards and 'to enter' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulars are members of a standing professional army, as opposed to reserves.

clue.text: Fuss over political party getting tense result in

indicators.note: over in the sense of covering, so the fuss is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: ado means fuss
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A row about a party getting nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is a Northern Irish political party.
explanation.definitionFit: If things amount to or lead to an outcome, they produce it as a consequence.

clue.text: Wages restored. Profits start after this

parts.note: wages are pay
something restored is back where it was
the full stop printed in the clue is a period in American usage

explanation.surface: Wages are reinstated, then a business remark that profits come later.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own full stop supplies PERIOD, a wordplay piece hiding as punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: In investment appraisal the payback period is the time taken to recover the outlay, after which a project yields gains.

clue.text: Drink and a piece of cake first

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An offer of a drink plus a slice of cake beforehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Kefir is a fermented milk beverage from the Caucasus.

clue.text: Beats first pair up for charity

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, applied only to the opening two letters of the word for beats, so they swap

parts.note: lams means beats or thrashes

explanation.surface: A first couple of hits raising money for good causes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first pair up' turns only the LA of LAMS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts of money or food to the poor, a form of almsgiving or benevolence.

clue.text: In small functions, remove ties

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: In tells us one piece is placed within the other pieces

explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' looks like parties but means mathematical tangents; 'In' sets the word for remove inside them, after the small.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-off is a deadlock or draw in which neither side wins, which is what a tie is.

clue.text: Bring about prime spots for timepieces before lake

explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or force something into motion, so to cause it or make it happen.

clue.text: Impersonate party animal no longer

parts.note: to do someone is to mimic or impersonate them
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Pretend to be a party animal, no longer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is the flightless Mauritian bird that became extinct in the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Religious houses bar one good — astonishing!

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so the bar and its companions go inside
